person.name: Henry_II
person.summary: Henry II (6 May 973 – 13 July 1024), also known as Saint Henry, was Duke of Bavaria, King of the Romans, King of Italy, and Holy Roman Emperor. The last ruler of the Ottonian dynasty, he consolidated royal power north of the Alps, relied heavily on the Church and episcopal administration, promoted monastic reform, founded the Diocese of Bamberg, and fought major wars against Bolesław I of Poland and rivals in Italy. Deeply pious and childless, he was canonized in 1146.

events.title: Contested accession and coronation as King of Germany (King of the Romans)
events.description: After the death of Emperor Otto III without heirs in January 1002 and a contested succession, Henry secured sufficient support to be anointed and crowned King of Germany (Rex Romanorum) by Archbishop Willigis at Mainz on 9 July 1002. He was the first German king to adopt the title King of the Romans prior to imperial coronation in Rome and the first since Otto I not to be crowned at Aachen.

images.caption: Medieval illumination depicting the coronation of Henry II as King of the Romans.

events.title: Cunigunde crowned Queen of Germany
events.description: Shortly after his own coronation, Henry arranged for Archbishop Willigis to crown his wife Cunigunde of Luxembourg as Queen of Germany at Paderborn on 10 August 1002. Her coronation formalized her role as Henry's consort and political partner within the kingdom.

images.caption: Relief showing Emperor Henry II with his wife Cunigunde.

events.title: Submission of Herman II of Swabia and consolidation of royal authority
events.description: After months of armed conflict and political struggle over the succession, Herman II, Duke of Swabia, was defeated near Strasbourg and on 1 October 1002 submitted to Henry II's authority. Though Herman retained the ducal title until his death, Henry effectively secured the recognition of his kingship across Swabia, strengthening his control over the duchies.

images.caption: Nineteenth-century depiction of Henry II presiding at a royal assembly, symbolizing his authority over the German nobility.

events.title: Anointed King of Italy at Pavia after first Italian expedition
events.description: Responding to appeals from Italian bishops opposed to the self-proclaimed king Arduin of Ivrea, Henry II led an expedition into northern Italy in 1004. After gaining the allegiance of many clergy and nobles and entering Pavia, he was anointed King of Italy (Rex Italiae) on 15 May 1004, reasserting German royal authority over the Italian kingdom.

images.caption: Political map of Italy around the year 1000, showing the fragmented territories over which Henry II claimed kingship.

events.date_note: Henry’s major conflicts with Bolesław I spanned much of his reign, culminating in the Peace of Bautzen in 1018
events.title: Prolonged wars and diplomacy with Bolesław I of Poland
events.description: From the early years of his reign Henry II engaged in a series of wars and negotiations with Bolesław I the Brave of Poland over control of Meissen, Lusatia, Bohemia, and other border regions. Campaigns, alliances, and truces alternated until the Peace of Bautzen in 1018 confirmed a compromise settlement. The Polish conflict dominated Henry’s foreign policy and highlighted his use of both military and diplomatic means.

locations.name_historic: Eastern Marches of the Holy Roman Empire

images.caption: Later depiction of Bolesław I the Brave, Henry II’s main Polish adversary.

events.title: Foundation of the Diocese of Bamberg
events.description: In 1007 Henry II founded the Diocese of Bamberg by elevating the region around Bamberg and endowing it with extensive lands, many taken from his own Bavarian and royal domains. The new bishopric strengthened royal control over eastern Franconia and served Henry's program of using the Church as a pillar of imperial administration and missionary work.

images.caption: Historical painting of the consecration of Bamberg Cathedral in the presence of Henry II and Cunigunde in 1007.

events.title: Issuance of royal and imperial charters under his signum manus
events.description: Throughout his reign Henry II issued numerous royal diplomas and charters granting privileges to churches, monasteries, and nobles. A charter from 1011 bearing his signum manus exemplifies his formal exercise of royal authority and close collaboration with ecclesiastical institutions in governance.

images.caption: Facsimile of Henry II’s signum manus on a charter issued in 1011.

events.title: Coronation as Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Benedict VIII
events.description: On 14 February 1014, during his second Italian expedition, Henry II was crowned Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Benedict VIII in Rome. The imperial coronation confirmed his position as emperor of the Romans and symbolized the alliance between the German monarchy and the papacy.

images.caption: Illumination showing Henry II being crowned Holy Roman Emperor by the pope.

events.title: Commission and donation of the Gospel Book of Henry II
events.description: Around the time of his imperial coronation, Henry II commissioned and donated a richly illuminated Gospel Book to the Church, reflecting his piety and patronage of Ottonian art. The manuscript, now known as the Gospel Book of Henry II, illustrates his desire to associate imperial rulership with liturgical splendour and monastic reform.

images.caption: Illuminated page from the Gospel Book of Henry II, commissioned for imperial liturgical use.

events.title: Death of Henry II at Grone
events.description: Henry II died on 13 July 1024 at Grone near Göttingen, having ruled as Holy Roman Emperor for a decade and as king for over twenty years. Childless, he was the last ruler of the Ottonian dynasty; after his death, the German princes elected Conrad II, initiating the Salian line of emperors.

images.caption: Tomb of Henry II and Cunigunde in Bamberg Cathedral.
